title: Study finds shorter prompts can cost more when models answer at greater length
friendlyTitle: Very short AI prompts may make answers longer and more expensive
summary: The CAVEWOMAN study tested eight models across five datasets and found that compressing model outputs reduced realised cost, while aggressively shortening user prompts raised average cost and reduced accuracy. The authors report that models often compensated for compressed input with longer answers.
friendlySummary: Researchers tested the idea of removing grammar and extra words from prompts. The shorter prompts often hurt accuracy and made models produce longer answers, while asking for shorter answers saved more money.
whyItMatters: Telegram-style prompts are not a guaranteed token-saving trick. Users and teams should optimise the whole exchange—clear input, requested output length, accuracy and total cost—rather than counting only the words sent to the model.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Clear instructions can be cheaper than cryptic ones when they prevent a long or confused reply. Ask for the answer length you need instead of cutting every useful word from the prompt.
